    [RNA, ATAC] [multiple RNA, multiple ATAC]

    Diagonal integration: [RNA, ATAC]¶

    Diagonal integration combines RNA and ATAC measured in different cells, with no pairing between them. If your RNA and ATAC come from the same cells, as in 10x Multiome, use the vertical tutorial. This tutorial runs iNMF and online_iNMF on D27mini, 3,000 RNA and 3,000 ATAC profiles of the benchmark dataset D27, then on data in your own format.

    Most diagonal methods read ATAC as gene-activity scores, made beforehand with a tool such as Signac or ArchR. GLUE and Seurat_v5 read the peak matrix, and MultiMAP and Seurat_v3 need both. Seurat_v5 also needs RNA and ATAC from the same cells. mtb.describe_layout("diagonal") lists each method's ATAC files.

    Methods run on Linux. On macOS or Windows, open this notebook in Colab.

    1. Install¶

    This cell installs multibench-sc. It keeps the numpy and pandas that are already installed, so Colab needs no restart.

    Details

    On Colab, choose a GPU runtime before you run the notebook: Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU. On a CPU runtime, an environment that has a smaller CPU build gets that build, and training methods run slower.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import numpy, pandas
pins = f"numpy=={numpy.__version__} pandas=={pandas.__version__}"
%pip install -q "multibench-sc>=0.3.7" {pins}
    import numpy, pandas pins = f"numpy=={numpy.__version__} pandas=={pandas.__version__}" %pip install -q "multibench-sc>=0.3.7" {pins}
    Note: you may need to restart the kernel to use updated packages.

    2. Download the data and the environments¶

    mtb.data.fetch downloads D27mini (15 MB) once. Each method runs in its own environment. mtb.env.install downloads the environments for iNMF and online_iNMF, with no conda needed. The download is 0.9 GB.

    Details

    state is PACKED for an environment downloaded now and have for one that was already there. Without dry_run=False, mtb.env.install downloads nothing and returns the plan with its sizes.

    Environments go to mtb.config.DEFAULT.envs_dir. To use another disk, set it before this cell.

    From a terminal, multibench env install --methods iNMF,online_iNMF --packed --run does the same.

    In [2]:

    import pandas as pd
import multibench as mtb

mtb.data.fetch("D27mini")

    3. Run the methods¶

    run_all runs each method on D27mini and scores its output with the scIB metrics. res.summary has one row per method with its status, run time and scores. Higher is better for every metric.

    Details

    Each method writes an embedding: a table of numbers with one row per cell. run_all scores it against the cell-type labels of D27mini.

    The clustering metrics ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1 and cLISI measure how well the embedding separates the cell types. The batch metrics ASW_batch, GC and iLISI measure how well the batches mix. They appear only when the data has several batches.

    res.failures says why a method failed. params={"Method": {"key": value}} sets a method's parameters, and mtb.params_for lists them. Many methods take none.

    mtb.load_batch("out/D27mini") reloads these results later without running anything.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    res = mtb.run_all("D27mini", "diagonal", methods=METHODS,
                  out_dir="out/D27mini")
res.summary

    4. Plot¶

    res.plot() draws the scores as a bubble table. Circle size shows the rank within a column, and bigger is better. The fill compares a value with the other rows in the same column.

    Details

    The lightest fill is the lowest value in this figure, not zero.

    Metrics are grouped by family: blue for dimension reduction and clustering, green for batch correction. Each family starts with an Overall bar. Its length and colour both show the family score.

    A column whose rows all hold the same value is drawn grey, and a warning names it. A figure of one method is grey everywhere.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    res.plot()
    res.plot()

    5. Your own data¶

    Your data needs raw RNA counts in one .h5ad file and ATAC in another, with a cell type for each cell in both. iNMF and online_iNMF read ATAC as gene-activity scores, and online_iNMF needs about 5,000 cells in total. Gene-activity scores are an ATAC matrix with one column per gene, as Signac or ArchR compute it.

    Starting from something else? See the recipes for labels in a CSV file and no labels.

    Details: export

    The names in quotes say where your file holds each part. "X" is the main matrix, "obsm:protein" the matrix obsm["protein"], "layer:counts" the layer layers["counts"], and "obs:celltype" the column obs["celltype"], which "celltype" alone names too. A wrong name after obsm:, layer: or obs: raises an error that lists the names the file has.

    The command line writes the same folder from the two files:

    multibench convert my_rna.h5ad mydata/MYDIAG_RNA_ATAC --rna X --atac-from my_atac.h5ad \
    --atac-kind gene_activity --labels obs:celltype --category diagonal

    labels= needs the column in both files. With cell types for the RNA cells only, leave labels= out and follow the recipe for no labels.

    For ATAC as a peak matrix, pass atac_kind="peak". GLUE and Seurat_v5 read peaks. mtb.describe_layout("diagonal") lists the files each method needs.

    NAME is the dataset name for scan and run_all, and mydata is the folder that holds it (data_path). With a new value of NAME, the folder holds the files of your data only.

    The check lists the methods you name. Without methods=, it lists every method that reads the modalities in the folder. Without per_method=True, it has one row per method variant and every column, such as the command of each method.

    export_dataset raises FileExistsError when the folder holds files of other cells that the call does not write. overwrite=True does not remove them. Give NAME a new value.

    overwrite=True replaces the files of an earlier run of this cell. Without it, export_dataset raises FileExistsError rather than replace a file.

    The cells below read your data, write it as a dataset folder, check the folder and run the same methods on it. So that the notebook runs as it is, the next cell writes two small example files, my_rna.h5ad and my_atac.h5ad, from 90% of the RNA profiles and 90% of the ATAC profiles of D27mini. It leaves a file of your own with one of those names as it is.

    Write the dataset folder. Change each name in quotes marked # <-: give NAME a new value, and write the names that your files use for the other parts. The printout above lists the names in your files. Write a name listed after obs: with that prefix, as "obs:celltype".

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    NAME = "MYDIAG_RNA_ATAC"   # <- a new name for your own data
mtb.io.export_dataset(rna, "mydata/" + NAME,
                      rna="X",                    # <- where the RNA counts are
                      atac=atac,                  # the ATAC file, values in X
                      atac_kind="gene_activity",  # <- or "peak"
                      labels="obs:celltype",      # <- the column in both files
                      category="diagonal", overwrite=True)
    NAME = "MYDIAG_RNA_ATAC" # <- a new name for your own data mtb.io.export_dataset(rna, "mydata/" + NAME, rna="X", # <- where the RNA counts are atac=atac, # the ATAC file, values in X atac_kind="gene_activity", # <- or "peak" labels="obs:celltype", # <- the column in both files category="diagonal", overwrite=True)

    PosixPath('mydata/MYDIAG_RNA_ATAC')

    Check the folder before you run anything. runnable says whether a method can run on your data on this computer, and reason says why not. The first two lines above the table say what the folder holds and how many cells each file has. Compare them with your data. A further line is about one method: why it cannot run, or what it does not read or needs from your data.

    6. Stored scores¶

    The package ships stored scores for 12 methods on D28. load_results reads them and mtb.plot.bubble draws them, without running anything.

    Details

    There are no stored scores for D27mini. D28 is another benchmark dataset of the same task.

    source="rerun" reads the package's own runs of the methods. source="published", the default, reads the published scIB tables, which hold 14 methods for D28.

    The stored scores used the leidenalg backend for Leiden clustering, and run_all uses igraph by default. The two backends can move ARI by up to about 0.1. To compare your runs with these scores, set mtb.config.DEFAULT.leiden_flavor = "leidenalg" before run_all.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    long = mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28", source="rerun")
mtb.plot.bubble(long)
    long = mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28", source="rerun") mtb.plot.bubble(long)
    /tmp/ipykernel_14292/4272824004.py:1: DegenerateRerunWarning: This re-run row has ARI below 0.01, while the published table has above 0.2 for the same method and dataset: Conos/D28 (re-run 0.2.1, ARI 0.0004). Such a row most likely comes from a failed re-run, for example a collapsed embedding or a wrong label order, not from the method itself. Drop it before ranking: df[df.method != 'Conos'].
  long = mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28", source="rerun")

    7. Every method of this task¶

    14 methods have a variant for diagonal [RNA, ATAC]. Each ran on D27mini in the package's own check, on a server with a GPU:

    Method Result Seconds
    Conos scored 42
    GLUE scored 340
    MultiMAP scored 23
    Portal scored 44
    SCALEX scored 261
    Seurat_v3 scored 51
    Seurat_v5 scored 357
    VIPCCA scored 10
    iNMF scored 18
    online_iNMF scored 8
    scBridge scored 26
    scJoint scored 28
    sciCAN scored 84
    uniPort scored 463

    To run them all, set METHODS to these names in section 2 and run the notebook again. That downloads 8 envs, 13.9 GB to download on a CPU host, 13.2 GB on a GPU host. This notebook does the same in Colab.

    Troubleshooting¶

    res.failures lists each method that failed or was skipped. Its error column ends with the method's error output.

    Details
    symptom fix
    env.install refuses on macOS or Windows methods run only on Linux: use Colab or a Linux machine
    a method needs an NVIDIA GPU choose a GPU runtime on Colab, or a machine with a GPU
    a method fails on a small dataset mtb.scan without per_method=True names what the method needs from the data's size in its caveat column
    a warning that values are not whole numbers export raw counts, for example with rna="layer:counts"
    ... matrix/data as cells x features the matrix is transposed: export it again with mtb.io.export_dataset
    a method times out raise timeout= in run_all
    low label_order_confidence several label files fit the cell count: check label_order_candidates in res.results
    batch metrics use the wrong batches res.rescore(batch=my_vector) scores again without running the methods
